function: CSI prediction: forecasting future compressed CSI frames at the BS from past frames fed back by the UE, with STNet compression and feedback, for massive MIMO (pp. 1-3).
system: Massive MIMO-OFDM; BS with [8,2,2] dual-polarized array (Nt=32), single-antenna UE, 32 subcarriers, 20 MHz, UMa; carrier frequency not stated (pp. 2-3, Table I).
method: STEM GNN (latent-correlation self-attention layer, GFT/DFT graph blocks) predicting compressed CSI, with STNet encoder; supervised, RMSE loss, RMSProp, 100 epochs, batch 50, learning rate 1e-4 (pp. 3, 5).
data_channel: Simulated 3GPP (TR 38.901) 3D channel, Urban Macro (UMa), 10,000 consecutive timestamps; no train/test split or dataset size stated (pp. 2-3, Table I).
test_conditions: UE mobility 3, 30, 120 km/h; compression ratios 1/16, 1/8, 1/4; horizons P; K=12; Eb/N0 0-30 dB; no train versus test condition split stated (pp. 3-4).
baselines: Learned only: RNN, LSTM, Transformer CSI predictors; STNet used for compression and feedback; no classical predictor (autoregression, extrapolation) or outdated-CSI baseline compared (p. 3).
metrics: Spectral efficiency with ZF precoding versus Eb/N0, mobility and compression ratio; RMSE of predicted CSI versus horizon; training loss; parameters and runtime (pp. 3-5).
complexity: Table II: parameters and runtime per channel usage; STEM GNN 1.87M parameters and 9.5 ms at C=512, versus transformer 1.72M parameters and 7.3 ms (p. 4).
openness: Source code released: https://github.com/sharanmourya/CSI-Prediction/ (footnote 1, p. 5); no data link.
q1_support: p. 2: "conforming to the specifications outlined in the 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) for 5G communications [12]"; p. 3: "simulations using the 3GPP channel model" (Table I: UMa); [12] is 3GPP TR 38.901 (p. 5).
q2_support: p. 4: "STEM GNN is equipped with enough representation power to generalize the compressed CSI for higher mobilities" is a performance claim; Table I (p. 3) lists one scenario (UMa) and no model trained under one condition and tested under another is stated. Not met.
q3_support: p. 3: "we compare our approach with RNN, LSTM and transformer-based CSI prediction models"; all are learned, and Figs. 3-5 and Table II show no non-learned predictor (autoregression, extrapolation, outdated CSI). Not met.
q4_support: p. 4: "we tabulated the number of parameters used by each approach along with the runtime of the model for a single channel usage"
notes: Title and DOI on p. 1 match the work. Tables I and II and Figs. 3-6 were read from the page images (pp. 3-5). The text gives no carrier frequency and no train/validation/test split. The generalization to higher mobility on p. 4 is claimed from the results over mobility, not from a stated train and test mismatch, so q2 is 0.
